mainTopic: Fixing mistakes with the blood in the משנה, and whether unfit and טמא people may slaughter a קרבן לכתחילה
overview: The משנה finishes its list of mistakes with the blood of a קרבן. If an unfit person collected the blood, or it was placed in the wrong spot, a fit כהן collects again, as long as דם הנפש is still flowing. This holds even if the unfit person collected with intent of חוץ לזמנו or חוץ למקומו, since the intent of someone unfit for the עבודה does not disqualify. If the blood only ended up in the wrong hand, person or vessel, it is simply put back. The גמרא then reads the past-tense word ששחטו and infers that unfit people should not slaughter לכתחילה. A ברייתא shows that a זר may slaughter even לכתחילה, so the גמרא explains that the past tense is only because of טמאים, who are kept away by a rabbinic גזירה so they do not touch the meat. Another ברייתא learns from סמיכה that שחיטה needs a טהור. The גמרא says this is only מדרבנן: a טמא can slaughter from outside the עזרה with a long knife, but he cannot do סמיכה, because putting his hands into the עזרה counts as entering. Finally, רב חסדא teaches the comparison the other way, and the גמרא begins to examine his version, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Collection that did not count can be redone
steps.stepSummary: If one of the unfit people collected the blood, a fit כהן collects again, as long as דם הנפש is still flowing. This is true even if they collected with intent of חוץ לזמנו or חוץ למקומו, because the intent of someone unfit for the עבודה does not disqualify.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of the unfit people who collected the blood with intent of beyond its time or outside its place: if lifeblood is still coming out of the animal, a fit כהן should go back and collect it properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה says that a bad collection of the blood is not the end of the קרבן. A fit כהן can simply collect again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קבלה by an unfit person simply does not count, so it can be done again if proper blood is still available, meaning דם הנפש and not just the last drips. Even a wrong intention of time or place does not ruin the קרבן here, because such intent disqualifies only when it comes from someone fit for the עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Collecting the blood of the קרבן in a vessel
Lifeblood, the blood that flows out while the animal is dying, as opposed to the last drips
Here: a כהן who is fit to do the עבודה
He should go back and collect again

steps.confusionAlert: Only דם הנפש counts. If all that is left is the slow dripping blood (דם התמצית), it cannot be collected again for the קרבן.

phrases.english: And all of them who collected the blood
phrases.notes: 'All of them' points back to the unfit people listed earlier in the משנה.

phrases.english: with intent of beyond its time or outside its place,
if there is lifeblood still in the animal,
the fit one should go back and collect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous daf, which listed unfit people who slaughtered
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A collection by an unfit person can be redone by a fit כהן if דם הנפש remains, even where the collection was done with intent of חוץ לזמנו or חוץ למקומו.

steps.title: Blood that ended up in the wrong place can be brought back
steps.stepSummary: If the blood was moved to an unfit person, to the left hand, or to a non-sacred vessel, it is returned to its proper place. Spilled blood that is gathered up is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a fit כהן collected the blood and handed it to an unfit person, it goes back to the fit כהן. If he collected it in his right hand and moved it to his left, it goes back to his right. If he collected it in a holy vessel and poured it into a plain vessel, it goes back into a holy vessel. If it spilled from the vessel onto the floor and he gathered it up, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives cases where a proper collection was done and then the blood ended up somewhere wrong. In each case you just put it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the קבלה itself was proper, so there is no need to collect again. The later mistake only interrupted the process, and returning the blood to its right state fixes it. Even blood that fell on the floor is not ruined once it is gathered up.

keyTerms.meaning: A person unfit for the עבודה
Right hand / left hand; the עבודה must be done with the right hand
A sanctified Temple vessel
An ordinary, non-sacred vessel
The floor of the עזרה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the difference between redoing a step that did not count (Step 1) and simply correcting where the blood ended up after a good step.

phrases.english: If the fit one collected and gave it to an unfit one,
he should return it to the fit one.
If he collected in his right hand and moved it to his left,
he should return it to his right.

phrases.aramaic: קִיבֵּל בִּכְלִי קֹדֶשׁ וְנָתַן לִכְלִי חוֹל –
phrases.english: If he collected in a holy vessel and put it in a plain vessel,
he should return it to a holy vessel.
If it spilled from the vessel onto the floor
and he gathered it up, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a collection that did not count to a good collection followed by a fixable mistake
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood that is moved to a wrong person, hand or vessel is simply returned, and gathered spilled blood is כשר.

steps.title: Blood placed in the wrong spot: collect again
steps.stepSummary: Blood placed on the כבש, not opposite the יסוד, above or below the חוט הסיקרא when it belongs on the other side, or inside or outside the היכל when it belongs on the other side, does not count. A fit כהן collects again if דם הנפש remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the blood was put on the ramp, or on a part of the מזבח not opposite the base, or blood meant for below the red line was put above it, or blood meant for above was put below, or blood meant for inside was put outside, or blood meant for outside was put inside, then if lifeblood is still coming out, a fit כהן should go back and collect again.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists wrong places to put the blood. Each mistake is fixed the same way: collect fresh blood, if possible, and do it properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the blood was already used up in the wrong spot, so it cannot just be moved back as in Step 2. Placing it wrongly simply does not count. That is why new blood must be collected, and that is only possible if דם הנפש is still flowing.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח
The base of the מזבח, which did not run along every side
Below / above the red line (חוט הסיקרא) on the מזבח
Inside the היכל / outside on the outer מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: There are two kinds of fix in the משנה. If the blood only ended up in the wrong place, you return it. If a step did not count (bad collection, wrong placement), you collect again, but only while דם הנפש is still flowing.

phrases.english: If he placed it on the ramp;
or not opposite the base;
phrases.notes: Some blood has to go on a part of the מזבח that has the יסוד below it.

phrases.english: if he put what is meant for below up above;
or what is meant for above down below;
or what is meant for inside outside;
or what is meant for outside inside;
if there is lifeblood,
the fit one should go back and collect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from mistakes in collecting and handling to mistakes in placing the blood
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood placed in the wrong spot does not count, and fresh blood is collected if דם הנפש remains.

steps.title: Inference: unfit people should not slaughter in the first place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the past-tense word שחטו and infers that שחיטה by unfit people is valid בדיעבד but not allowed לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה said 'they slaughtered,' in the past tense. That means after the fact, yes, it is valid. But from the start, no, they should not slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by drawing an inference from the wording at the start of the משנה, 'all unfit people who slaughtered.' This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A past-tense ruling ('if they did it, it works') suggests it is only valid בדיעבד, after it already happened. So the inference is that unfit people should not be asked to slaughter לכתחילה. The גמרא will go on to examine this claim.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They slaughtered' (past tense)
After the fact, once it was already done
From the start, as the proper way to act
Yes / no

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say their שחיטה is invalid. It is valid. The point is only that it should not be done this way from the start.

phrases.english: Gemara: 'They slaughtered':
phrases.notes: This quotes the opening of the משנה on the previous daf, 'כל הפסולין ששחטו.'

phrases.english: after the fact, yes,
from the start, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא by going back to the first word of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the past tense שחטו: unfit people's שחיטה is valid בדיעבד, but they should not slaughter לכתחילה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says slaughter by non-priests is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 4's inference with a ברייתא that says שחיטה is valid when done by a זר, women, slaves, or טמאים, even for קדשי קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction: 'And he shall slaughter' teaches that slaughter by a non-priest is valid, for slaughter is valid by non-priests, women, slaves, and impure people, even for the most sacred offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to clash with what it just inferred from the משנה. This step opens a challenge that the next steps will develop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said שחיטה by unfit people is only בדיעבד, because the משנה used the past tense. This ברייתא states flatly that שחיטה is כשרה by a זר and others, which sounds like a normal, allowed practice. That sets up a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction. This introduces a source that seems to clash with what was just said.
A non-כהן.
The most holy category of קרבנות.
People who are ritually impure.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
'And he shall slaughter': slaughter by a non-priest is valid,
for slaughter is valid by non-priests
and by women, by slaves, and by impure people.
And even with the most sacred offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference made in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 4's inference that שחיטה by unfit people is only valid בדיעבד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא describes שחיטה by a זר as simply valid, which suggests it is permitted even לכתחילה.

steps.title: The ברייתא asks whether slaughter might be limited to priests
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether perhaps only כהנים may slaughter, and it names the source for that idea: the פסוק giving the כהנים charge over 'every matter of the altar.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is only by priests? You might say so, and where would you get that idea? From the verse: 'And you and your sons with you shall guard your priesthood for every matter of the altar.'
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, a possible objection is raised: maybe שחיטה belongs only to כהנים. The ברייתא also explains where that idea would come from, which sets up its answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in במדבר says the כהנים are in charge of 'every matter of the altar.' On a plain reading, that could include שחיטה. The ברייתא states this possibility clearly so that it can reject it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only. This raises a possible alternative reading.
From the fact that it says.
The priesthood and its exclusive roles.

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is only by priests?
You can reply: from where did you come to this idea?
From the fact that it says:
'And you and your sons with you'
'shall guard your priesthood'
'for every matter of the altar';

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא by testing its claim against a פסוק that seems to support limiting the job to כהנים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether שחיטה is limited to כהנים because of the general פסוק about the כהנים' charge over the altar.

steps.title: The verse shows the priests' job starts at collecting the blood
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves from ויקרא 1:5 that the כהנים' exclusive role begins at קבלה. So שחיטה is valid by any person.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think this applies even to slaughter? The verse teaches: 'And he shall slaughter the young bull before ה׳, and [בני אהרן הכהנים] shall bring close.' From collecting onward it is a מצוה of the priesthood. This teaches about slaughter that it is valid by any person.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The פסוק names the כהנים only after the slaughter, so שחיטה is open to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, 'and he shall slaughter' has no mention of כהנים. Then 'בני אהרן הכהנים shall bring close' starts with the blood. So the general rule of 'every matter of the altar' covers only קבלה and the stages after it. Saying שחיטה is valid 'by any person' sounds like it is fully allowed, and that sharpens the contradiction with Step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought. This introduces a possibility that will be rejected.
The verse teaches.
Collecting the blood in a sacred vessel. This is the first job reserved for כהנים.
A task that only כהנים may perform.

steps.whatToRemember: Only the stages from קבלה onward belong exclusively to כהנים. שחיטה is valid by anyone.

phrases.english: One might think this applies even to slaughter?
The verse teaches:
'And he shall slaughter the young bull before ה׳'
'and they shall bring close, etc.'
phrases.notes: The פסוק goes on 'בני אהרן הכהנים,' so the כהנים are named only after the slaughter (ויקרא 1:5).

phrases.english: From collecting the blood onward, it is a מצוה of the priesthood;
this taught about slaughter
that it is valid by any person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Step 6 and completes the ברייתא used for the challenge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק names the כהנים only from קבלה onward, so שחיטה is valid by any person.

steps.title: Non-priests may slaughter from the start; the past tense is because of impure people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a זר may slaughter even לכתחילה. The משנה used the past tense 'ששחטו' only because it also lists טמאים, who are kept from slaughtering לכתחילה so they do not touch the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same rule applies even from the outset. But because the משנה wants to teach about impure people, who may not slaughter from the outset because of a decree that they might touch the meat, it taught 'that they slaughtered.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. It takes back the idea from Step 4 for a זר and explains the past tense through the case of טמאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is right: a זר, women, and slaves may slaughter even לכתחילה. Only טמאים are kept away, because of a rabbinic גזירה that they might touch the meat and make it impure. Since one wording had to cover the whole list, the משנה used the past tense to fit the טמאים.

keyTerms.meaning: The same rule applies.
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard.
Lest they touch the meat and make it impure.

steps.whatToRemember: A זר may slaughter a קרבן even לכתחילה. Only a טמא is kept away לכתחילה, by rabbinic decree. The past tense in the משנה was chosen because of the טמאים.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not keep Step 4's conclusion for a זר. The past-tense wording does not limit a זר to בדיעבד. It reflects only the rule for טמאים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the wording of a משנה can be shaped by one item on its list. A careful inference from the wording can be overturned once we see which case forced that wording.

phrases.english: The same rule applies even from the outset too;
but because it wants to teach about impure people,
who may not slaughter from the outset,
because of a decree lest they touch the meat;
it taught: 'that they slaughtered.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction between the ברייתא (Steps 5-7) and the inference from the משנה (Step 4).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה: the past tense is driven by one item in the list.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The past tense 'ששחטו' means that שחיטה by any unfit person is only בדיעבד.
steps.terutzMaskana: A זר may slaughter לכתחילה. Only טמאים are kept away לכתחילה, because of a גזירה that they might touch the meat, and that is why the משנה used the past tense.

steps.title: Is an impure person's slaughter really valid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that a טמא's שחיטה is valid, quoting a ברייתא that links שחיטה to סמיכה, which must be done by טהורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really fine, after the fact, when a טמא slaughters? But there is a contradicting source: 'And he shall place his hand… and he shall slaughter.' Just as placing hands is done only by pure people, so slaughter must be done only by pure people!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last step, which said a טמא's שחיטה works. It brings a source showing that שחיטה needs a pure person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה writes סמיכה and שחיטה right next to each other, so the ברייתא compares them. Since סמיכה needs a טהור, שחיטה should need one too. That clashes with the ruling that a טמא's שחיטה is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contradicted: a source is brought that conflicts with what was just said
Leaning one's hands on the head of the קרבן before it is slaughtered
People who are ritually pure
It is fine after the fact

phrases.english: And an impure person, after the fact, is it fine?!
But they raised a contradiction: 'And he shall place… and he shall slaughter'
just as placing hands is by pure people,
so too slaughter is by pure people!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption in Step 8 that a טמא's שחיטה is valid בדיעבד.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that שחיטה by a טמא is valid after the fact.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא compares שחיטה to סמיכה, which needs a טהור, so a טמא's שחיטה should be invalid.

steps.title: The requirement is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The rule that only טהורים may slaughter is מדרבנן. By תורה law a טמא's שחיטה is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is only a rabbinic rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in one word: the ברייתא's rule that שחיטה needs a pure person comes from the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By תורה law a טמא's שחיטה stands, so the earlier ruling holds. The ברייתא's link to סמיכה is only rabbinic support. This fits Step 8: the חכמים kept טמאים away so they would not touch the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: From rabbinic law, not from the תורה itself

phrases.english: By rabbinic law.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Downgrades the source's rule from תורה law to rabbinic law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means a טמא's שחיטה is invalid by תורה law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The requirement is only מדרבנן, so בדיעבד the שחיטה is valid.

steps.title: Both say 'before ה׳', so why the difference?
steps.stepSummary: If סמיכה needs a טהור by תורה law because it is 'לפני ה׳', then שחיטה should too, since it also says 'לפני ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about placing hands? That it says 'before ה׳.' But slaughter also says 'before ה׳'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why סמיכה would need a pure person by תורה law but שחיטה would not. Both happen 'לפני ה׳.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לפני ה׳' means in the עזרה, and a טמא may not enter the עזרה. That explains why a טמא cannot do סמיכה. But the same words appear about שחיטה, so a טמא should not be able to slaughter either.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why treat these two cases differently?
Before ה׳: in the עזרה, where a טמא may not enter

steps.confusionAlert: The problem with a טמא here is not his touch. The problem is that he may not enter the עזרה, which is where 'לפני ה׳' happens.

phrases.english: What is different about placing hands?
That it is written: 'Before the Lord';
phrases.notes: 'Before the Lord' means inside the עזרה, and a טמא isn't allowed in there.

phrases.english: Slaughter too, isn't it written: 'Before the Lord'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 10's split between סמיכה (תורה law) and שחיטה (rabbinic).
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only סמיכה, and not שחיטה, needs a טהור by תורה law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both have 'לפני ה׳', which keeps a טמא out of the עזרה, so both should need a טהור.

steps.title: A long knife from outside
steps.stepSummary: A טמא can slaughter without entering the עזרה by using a long knife from outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible: he makes a long knife and slaughters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a טמא can do שחיטה while standing outside the עזרה, reaching in with a long knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לפני ה׳' for שחיטה requires the animal to be in the עזרה, not the person slaughtering. So the person can be טמא if he stays outside. For סמיכה there is no such trick, as the next steps discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: A long knife
It is possible

phrases.english: It is possible that he makes a long knife
and slaughters.
phrases.notes: He stands outside the עזרה and reaches the animal inside with the knife.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a practical case where the טמא never enters the עזרה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לפני ה׳' for שחיטה forces the slaughterer to enter the עזרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A טמא can slaughter from outside with a long knife.

steps.title: Couldn't he just reach his hands in for סמיכה?
steps.stepSummary: The same trick should work for סמיכה: the טמא stands outside and puts only his hands in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Placing hands too: it is possible that he puts his hands in and places them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: if a long knife works for שחיטה, a טמא could also do סמיכה by reaching only his hands into the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge uses the same logic as Step 12. If staying mostly outside solves the problem for שחיטה, it should solve it for סמיכה too. Then the difference between them disappears again.

keyTerms.meaning: He brings his hands inside

phrases.english: Placing hands too:
it is possible that he puts his hands in and places them.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְמִיכָה נָמֵי – אֶפְשָׁר דִּמְעַיֵּיל יְדֵיהּ וְסָמֵיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses Step 12's own logic to challenge the difference between סמיכה and שחיטה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference between סמיכה and שחיטה for a טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a טמא can slaughter from outside, he can also do סמיכה from outside by reaching in his hands.

steps.title: Partial entry counts as entry
steps.stepSummary: The תנא holds that putting part of the body into the עזרה counts as entering, so a טמא's hands may not go in.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that a partial entry is called an entry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that putting even your hands into the עזרה counts as entering it. So a טמא cannot do סמיכה that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a long knife, no part of the body enters, only the knife. With סמיכה, the hands themselves must touch the animal, and hands going in count as the person entering. That is the real difference between the two.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this opinion)
Entering with part of the body is considered entering

steps.whatToRemember: By תורה law a טמא may slaughter a קרבן with a long knife from outside, but he cannot do סמיכה. Putting his hands into the עזרה counts as entering. The ban on a טמא doing שחיטה is only מדרבנן.

phrases.english: He holds
phrases.notes: 'He' is the תנא of the ברייתא from Step 9.

phrases.english: that a partial entry is called an entry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13 and closes this line of questions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a legal principle that separates the two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Reaching only the hands in does not count as entering.
steps.terutzMaskana: Partial entry counts as entry, so סמיכה by a טמא is impossible. A knife is not part of the body, so שחיטה is possible.

steps.title: רב חסדא teaches the comparison the other way
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא's version of the ברייתא reverses the comparison: just as שחיטה needs טהורים, so does סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא taught it the opposite way: 'And he shall place… and he shall slaughter.' Just as slaughter is by pure people, so too placing hands is by pure people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב חסדא's version of the same ברייתא. In his version, שחיטה is the source and סמיכה learns from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, סמיכה was the clear case that needs a טהור, and שחיטה was learned from it. רב חסדא flips this. In his version, needing a pure person is the starting rule for שחיטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the ברייתא quoted in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב חסדא's version, שחיטה needs טהורים, and סמיכה is learned from שחיטה.

steps.title: Why does שחיטה need a pure person in רב חסדא's version?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes שחיטה special in רב חסדא's version, and starts to answer: it says 'לפני ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about slaughter? That it is written: 'Before ה׳'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to examine רב חסדא's version. It asks why שחיטה would need a טהור, and points to 'לפני ה׳.' This sets up the next move, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'לפני ה׳' is used to explain why שחיטה needs a pure person, since a טמא may not enter the עזרה. The reader should expect the same kind of back-and-forth as before, now applied to רב חסדא's version.

phrases.english: What is different about slaughter?
That it is written: 'Before the Lord',

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why שחיטה, in רב חסדא's version, needs a טהור.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because it says 'לפני ה׳', meaning the עזרה, which a טמא may not enter. The discussion continues on the next amud.
